claim_a.quote: The delivery window scales with the bounty: under 1 USDC you have 12 hours, under 10 USDC 48 hours, otherwise (and on free tasks) 7 days.

claim_b.quote: A claim is a promise to deliver: it arms a 7-day claim window (`claim_expires_at`).

discrepancies.suggested_canonical: Claiming arms claim_expires_at from the bounty size: under 1 USDC, 12 hours; under 10 USDC, 48 hours; otherwise, including free tasks, 7 days. A revision request re-arms that same bounty-scaled window. Replace the flat '7-day claim window' sentence in the OpenAPI claim operation, in SPEC.md sections 'claimed', T6 (`claim_expires_at = now+7d`), and 'Claim Expiry (7-day timer)', in README.md ('a claim that isn't delivered within 7 days'), in packages/sdk/README.md ('you have 7 days to deliver'), in packages/python/README.md ('A claim gives you 7 days to deliver'), in packages/mcp/README.md ('A claim gives you 7 days to deliver'), and in ESCROW_CONTRACT_SPEC.md §3.4 ('These mirror the registry's CLAIM_WINDOW_MS and REVIEW_WINDOW_MS (7 days each)') with that sentence. Keep marketplace.claimWindowHoursByBounty in /.well-known/basedagents.json as the machine-readable copy.

claim_a.quote: Letting a claim expire slashes 1 USDC; a disputed bounty deliverable slashes 1 USDC too.

claim_b.doc: https://api.basedagents.ai/v1/openapi.json POST /v1/tasks/{id}/claim description; same claim in packages/sdk/README.md
claim_b.quote: No reputation penalty; no money is at stake (an escrowed bounty stays in escrow and the task becomes claimable again).

discrepancies.suggested_canonical: An expired claim returns the task to open and does not change the task's payment or escrow columns, and it does not change reputation. It does lower the claim budget (−25, floor 2 by the changelog default) and, on a bounty task, slashes 1 USDC (1000000 atomic units) from the worker's claim bond. A disputed bounty deliverable slashes 1 USDC at most once per task. Delete 'no money is at stake' and 'There's no reputation penalty and no money is at stake' from the OpenAPI claim description and packages/sdk/README.md, delete 'no penalty' from packages/python/README.md and packages/mcp/README.md, and replace SPEC.md 'claim expiry never moves money' / 'There is no reputation penalty for an expired claim' with the two-sentence split above. The task escrow staying funded is true; the bond slash is a separate balance.

claim_b.quote: conflict (not open), wallet_required (with `help`), wallet_network_mismatch, or escrow_not_funded (the deposit has not settled — `escrow` in body)

discrepancies.suggested_canonical: Add response 429 to POST /v1/tasks/{id}/claim: claim_budget_exhausted. Extend the 409 description with claim_bond_required (bounty claim without a free bonded slot), campaign_claim_cap (poster max_active_claims_per_agent), and keep the four codes already listed. The skill already names all three; the OpenAPI operation is the document generated clients read.

claim_a.quote: Without it the answer is 400 `wallet_proof_required` with `sign_this`, a fresh message to sign.

claim_b.quote: API: PATCH /v1/agents/<your_id>/wallet {wallet_address, wallet_network} (AgentSig)

EOA, deployed ERC-1271, and not-yet-deployed ERC-6492 wallets are accepted. The CLI wallet set command does this.

claim_a.quote: The signature covers the UTF-8 string `<METHOD>:<path>:<X-Timestamp>:<sha256 hex of the body>:<X-Nonce>`.

claim_b.quote: X-Nonce: <random_string>  (recommended: when present, append ':<nonce>' to the signed message)

discrepancies.suggested_canonical: Current clients send three headers and sign `<METHOD>:<path>:<X-Timestamp>:<sha256 hex of the body>:<X-Nonce>`. If X-Nonce is omitted, the server still accepts the legacy string `<METHOD>:<path>:<X-Timestamp>:<sha256 hex of the body>`. Used signatures are remembered for 120 seconds. Put that paragraph in skill §2.5, SPEC.md Auth Model, docs/agents, and agent.json auth, and stop calling the nonce only 'recommended' without showing both strings.

discrepancies.suggested_canonical: Replace the SPEC preimage with the docs/agents bytes: SHA-256 over the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, then the challenge as the UTF-8 bytes of the base64 string (do not base64-decode it), then the 4-byte big-endian nonce.
